attempts.error: The Antrieb managed cluster lease expired at 2026-09-04T21:43:07.158000+00:00

diagnosis.summary: The evidence shows the task was actually completed successfully: by 21:42:07 all four nodes reported a synced 4-member Galera cluster in Primary state, with pre-existing data intact and writes made on both node2 and node4 replicated cluster-wide, and the cluster survived a full rolling reboot of all four nodes. The attempt terminated not from a functional failure but because the cluster lease expired at 21:43:07, about a minute after the last successful verification, before a structured report could be returned. Time was likely lost earlier to a failed privileged file write (heredoc redirect without sudo/tee) and RHEL7/MariaDB-10.6 package dependency resolution problems (missing rsync/perl-Socket chains) plus yum installs exceeding the platform's 120s proxy timeout.

evidence.finding: `cat > /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb.repo <<EOF` failed with 'Permission denied' on node1-4; the repo file was never created via this command.
yum install failed with unresolved deps: MariaDB-server-10.6.28 requires rsync and perl(Socket), neither present.
Manual install of rsync/perl-Socket RPMs from vault.centos.org failed on further missing perl module deps (MODULE_COMPAT, Carp, Exporter, etc.).
`yum install -y MariaDB-server ... galera-4 rsync nc` exceeded the platform's 120s proxy read timeout and were reported as 'failed', though the command may have continued server-side.
Immediately after the timeout, rpm -q shows MariaDB-server/galera-4 still NOT installed on node4.
By this point node1 does show MariaDB-server-10.6.28 and galera-4-26.4.27 installed, with libgalera_smm.so present — so installation eventually succeeded on at least node1.
`mysql -e ...` returned 'ERROR 1045: Access denied for user root@localhost' — auth was not yet in a usable state at that point.
wsrep_cluster_size=4, wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced, wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, and `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM appdb.orders` returns 5 rows.

Each node was rebooted, came back with a new boot_id, mariadb.service reported active, and each independently reported wsrep_cluster_size=4/Synced/Primary with 5 rows in appdb.orders — cluster survived a rolling reboot of all four nodes.

wsrep_incoming_addresses lists all 4 node IPs; appdb.orders contains rows explicitly tagged 'WrittenOnNode2' and 'WrittenOnNode4', confirming multi-master writes were accepted and replicated across the 4-node cluster.
Lease expired at 21:43:07, about one minute after the last successful verification command and with no structured report returned.

likely_causes.cause: The task was functionally completed — a 4-node Galera cluster (node1-4) was running, synced, Primary, with pre-existing and node-local writes replicated everywhere, and it survived a full rolling reboot — but the attempt ran out of lease time before the executor could submit its structured completion report.

Early time was lost to two friction points: (1) a heredoc redirect into /etc/yum.repos.d/ without sudo/tee, which silently failed and had to be reworked, and (2) RHEL7/MariaDB-10.6 dependency resolution requiring manual RPM fetches from vault.centos.org for rsync/perl-Socket, which itself hit further unresolved perl module deps.

Foreground `yum install` calls for the full MariaDB+Galera package set on node3/node4 exceeded the platform's 120-second proxy read timeout, which likely triggered retries or re-verification steps that consumed additional lease time even though the install may have completed server-side.
A transient root@localhost auth issue on node2 (Access denied) required extra troubleshooting before verification could proceed, though it was resolved by 21:40:56.

next_attempt_guidance: Write privileged files via `sudo tee /etc/yum.repos.d/mariadb.repo` (or write to /tmp then `sudo mv`) instead of a bare heredoc redirect — the redirect itself is not run as root even inside an exec that has sudo available.

For MariaDB-10.6 on RHEL7, expect rsync and perl(Socket)-family packages to be missing from base repos; either enable EPEL/vault.centos.org base repos first or pre-stage the full perl dependency chain (Carp, Exporter, XSLoader, strict, warnings::register) rather than pulling rsync/perl-Socket one-off.

Run `yum install` for the full MariaDB+Galera package set in background with output redirected to a log file and poll it, per the platform's streaming-command pattern, rather than a single foreground call — this avoids the 120s proxy timeout seen on node3/node4 and avoids ambiguity about whether the install actually completed.

Verify package install state explicitly (`rpm -q MariaDB-server galera-4`) on every node immediately after each install step before moving on, since one node silently lagged behind the others in this attempt.
Use `sudo mysql` (unix_socket auth) for verification instead of `mysql -u root -p...` to avoid the transient 'Access denied for root@localhost' seen on node2.

Budget lease time conservatively: this attempt reached full success (4/4 nodes Synced+Primary, cross-node writes replicated, survived rolling reboot) but the lease expired ~60s later with no report submitted — submit the structured completion report as soon as the success criteria are confirmed rather than doing additional optional checks.

The working end-state pattern (bootstrap node1-3, join node4 via wsrep_cluster_address pointing at the existing 3, then verify writes from node2 and node4 replicate cluster-wide) is validated by this run's final checks and can be reused directly on a fresh cluster.
